import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from slugkit.core import slugify

def test():
    # Acceptance criteria
    assert slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world'
    assert slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b'
    assert slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three'
    assert slugify('x___y') == 'x-y'
    assert slugify('end!') == 'end'
    assert slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded'
    assert slugify('--both--') == 'both'
    assert slugify('(parens)') == 'parens'
    assert slugify('') == ''
    assert slugify('!!!') == ''
    assert slugify('   ') == ''
    assert slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world'
    assert slugify('already-a-slug') == 'already-a-slug'
    assert slugify('Python 3') == 'python-3'
    assert slugify('MiXeD CaSe 42') == 'mixed-case-42'
    assert slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me'
    assert slugify('日日本語') == ''  # Note: original had Japanese characters; we need to use correct unicode
    # Actually the criterion: '\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e' which is '日本語'
    assert slugify('日本語') == ''
    # Ensure result is always str
    assert isinstance(slugify('test'), str)
    # TypeError for non-string
    for bad in (None, 3, 2.5, ['a'], b'bytes'):
        try:
            slugify(bad)
            print(f'Failed to raise for {bad}')
            return False
        except TypeError:
            pass
    print('All tests passed')
    return True

if test():
    sys.exit(0)
else:
    sys.exit(1)
